candidates.exact_span: "Water Quality Standards for Salinity - Colorado River System" by the Colorado River Basin Salinity Control Forum.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This references an external salinity standard regime for the Colorado River system. candidates.exact_span: Should the State adopt a State water quality standard, and/or develop or amend a TMDL, this permit may be reopened to establish effluent limitations for the parameter(s) to be consistent with that approved State standard and/or water quality management plan, in accordance with 40 CFR §122.44(d).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The passage conditions future establishment of effluent limitations on state standard adoption or TMDL action. Interpreting whether applicable numeric limits are already fixed versus contingent on reopening could change which parameters have enforceable limits for FY2025 measurement comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: the permit may be reopened and modified during the life of the permit if relevant procedures implementing the Water Quality Standards are either revised or promulgated by the New Mexico Environment Department.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Permit reopening tied to revised or promulgated WQS implementation procedures could alter both effluent limits and associated monitoring conditions mid-permit term. Whether such revisions are treated as operative for FY2025 could change limit applicability (A) and which monitoring obligations were in force (B).

candidates.exact_span: Modification of the permit is subject to the provisions of 40 CFR §124.5.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cited Part 124 modification procedures govern when and how permit changes become effective. Different readings of what modifications were legally in effect during FY2025 could change which limits (A) and monitoring requirements (B) are treated as binding.

candidates.exact_span: No variance requests have been received.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This states the variance status at the time of the fact sheet. Interpreting whether no variances were in effect for FY2025 (versus none merely received at drafting) affects whether alternative or relaxed numeric limits apply instead of standard permit limits.

candidates.exact_span: The permit is in the process of certification by the State agency following regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §124.53.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Certification status bears on when state-issued permit conditions become enforceable. If certification timing is read as leaving conditions provisional or unresolved for part of FY2025, that could change which limits and monitoring duties apply (A, B) and whether missing-evidence cases must be classified as unresolved rather than as established no-requirement or no-discharge states (C).

candidates.exact_span: New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Water, 20.6.4 NMAC, effective September 12, 2018.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This identifies the operative state water quality standards used to develop the permit. Different interpretations of which parameters and criteria from 20.6.4 NMAC were translated into enforceable effluent limits could change applicable numeric limits for reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: EPA approved TMDL for the San Juan River Watershed (Part One)-Navajo Nation Boundary at the HogBack to Navajo Dam, May 10, 2005.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The cited TMDL is listed as a basis for permit development. Interpreting which TMDL allocations or load reductions were implemented as numeric effluent limitations could change which limits apply to discharges in that watershed during FY2025.
